recs.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: A simple regularization method is presented, subword regularization, which trains the model with multiple subword segmentations probabilistically sampled during training, and a new sub word segmentation algorithm based on a unigram language model is proposed.

recs.title: Learn Your Tokens: Word-Pooled Tokenization for Language Modeling
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This paper considers an alternative 'learn your tokens' scheme which utilizes the word boundary to pool bytes/characters into word representations, which are fed to the primary language model, before again decoding individual characters/bytes per word in parallel.

recs.title: UTF-8 Plumbing: Byte-level Tokenizers Unavoidably Enable LLMs to Generate Ill-formed UTF-8
recs.venue: arXiv.org
recs.summary: This paper formalizes tokenization using monoid theory and proves that tokenizers whose vocabularies contain tokens that are ill-formed UTF-8 can always produce sequences that are ill-formed UTF-8.

recs.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper introduces a simpler and more effective approach, making the NMT model capable of open-vocabulary translation by encoding rare and unknown words as sequences of subword units, and empirically shows that subword models improve over a back-off dictionary baseline for the WMT 15 translation tasks English-German and English-Russian by 1.3 BLEU.

recs.title: Retrofitting (Large) Language Models with Dynamic Tokenization
recs.venue: arXiv.org
recs.summary: This work proposes retrofitting LMs with dynamic tokenization: a way to dynamically decide on token boundaries based on the input text via a subword-merging algorithm inspired by byte-pair encoding that can mitigate the limitations of static tokenization.

recs.title: Inducing Character-level Structure in Subword-based Language Models with Type-level Interchange Intervention Training
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work develops a causal intervention framework to learn robust and interpretable character representations inside subword-based language models and introduces a suite of character-level tasks that systematically vary in their dependence on meaning and sequence-level context.

recs.title: Tokenization is Sensitive to Language Variation
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: It is found that the best tokenizer varies on the two task types and that the pre-tokenizer has the biggest overall impact on performance, which encourages more work on language variation and its relation to tokenizers and thus LLM performance.

recs.title: Multi-view Subword Regularization
recs.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: To take full advantage of different possible input segmentations, the proposed Multi-view Subword Regularization (MVR) method enforces the consistency of predictors between using inputs tokenized by the standard and probabilistic segmentations.

recs.title: Byte Pair Encoding is Suboptimal for Language Model Pretraining
recs.venue: Findings
recs.summary: Differences between BPE and unigram LM tokenization are analyzed, finding that the latter method recovers subword units that align more closely with morphology and avoids problems stemming from BPE’s greedy construction procedure.

recs.title: BPE-Dropout: Simple and Effective Subword Regularization
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: BPE-dropout is introduced - simple and effective subword regularization method based on and compatible with conventional BPE that stochastically corrupts the segmentation procedure of BPE, which leads to producing multiple segmentations within the same fixed BPE framework.

recs.title: Tokenizer Choice For LLM Training: Negligible or Crucial?
recs.venue: NAACL-HLT
recs.summary: A comprehensive study on the influence of tokenizer choice on LLM downstream performance by training 24 mono- and multilingual LLMs at a 2.6B parameter scale, finding that the common tokenizer evaluation metrics fertility and parity are not always predictive of model downstream performance, rendering these metrics a questionable proxy for the model's downstream performance.

recs.title: SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models
recs.venue: arXiv.org
recs.summary: A "superword"tokenizer, SuperBPE, is introduced, which incorporates a simple pretokenization curriculum into the byte-pair encoding (BPE) algorithm to first learn subwords, then superwords that bridge whitespace, resulting in segmentations of text that are more uniform in per-token difficulty.

recs.title: Greed is All You Need: An Evaluation of Tokenizer Inference Methods
recs.venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)
recs.summary: It is shown that for the most commonly used tokenizers, greedy inference performs surprisingly well; and that SaGe, a recently-introduced contextually-informed tokenizer, outperforms all others on morphological alignment.

recs.title: SpaceByte: Towards Deleting Tokenization from Large Language Modeling
recs.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
recs.summary: SpaceByte is a novel byte-level decoder architecture that closes the performance gap between byte-level and subword autoregressive language modeling and outperforms other byte-level architectures and roughly matches the performance of tokenized Transformer architectures.

recs.title: Broken Tokens? Your Language Model can Secretly Handle Non-Canonical Tokenizations
recs.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
recs.summary: This work investigates the robustness of LMs to text encoded with non-canonical tokenizations entirely unseen during training, and identifies settings where non-canonical tokenization schemes can *improve* performance.

recs.title: Beyond Text Compression: Evaluating Tokenizers Across Scales
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: It is shown that smaller models can accurately predict significant differences in tokenizer impact on larger models at a fraction of the compute cost, and proposes new intrinsic tokenizer metrics inspired by Zipf's law that correlate more strongly with downstream performance than text compression when modeling unseen languages.

recs.title: An Analysis of BPE Vocabulary Trimming in Neural Machine Translation
recs.venue: First Workshop on Insights from Negative Results in NLP
recs.summary: It is indicated that, across a large space of hyperparameter settings, vocabulary trimming fails to consistently improve model performance, and is even prone to incurring heavy degradation.

recs.title: Stop Taking Tokenizers for Granted: They Are Core Design Decisions in Large Language Models
recs.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper reframes tokenization as a core modeling decision rather than a preprocessing step, and argues for a context-aware framework that integrates tokenizer and model co-design, guided by linguistic, domain, and deployment considerations.

recs.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: SentencePiece, a language-independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer designed for Neural-based text processing, finds that it is possible to achieve comparable accuracy to direct subword training from raw sentences.

recs.title: Tokenization Is More Than Compression
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: The hypothesis that fewer tokens lead to better downstream performance is found not to be the case, and PathPiece is introduced, a new tokenizer that segments a document’s text into the minimum number of tokens for a given vocabulary.

recs.title: MYTE: Morphology-Driven Byte Encoding for Better and Fairer Multilingual Language Modeling
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This work introduces a new paradigm that encodes the same information with segments of consistent size across diverse languages, based on morphemes, as their inventories are more balanced across languages than characters, which are used in previous methods.

recs.title: Analyzing Cognitive Plausibility of Subword Tokenization
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: This work presents a new evaluation paradigm that focuses on the cognitive plausibility of subword tokenization, and analyzes the correlation of the tokenizer output with the response time and accuracy of human performance on a lexical decision task.

recs.title: Zero-Shot Tokenizer Transfer
recs.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
recs.summary: A hypernetwork is trained taking a tokenizer as input and predicting the corresponding embeddings, which comes close to the original models' performance in cross-lingual and coding tasks while markedly reducing the length of the tokenized sequence.

recs.title: MAGNET: Improving the Multilingual Fairness of Language Models with Adaptive Gradient-Based Tokenization
recs.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems

recs.title: MrT5: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Byte-level Language Models
recs.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
recs.summary: MrT5 is introduced, a more efficient variant of ByT5 that integrates a token deletion mechanism in its encoder to dynamically shorten the input sequence length, and presents a solution to the practical limitations of existing byte-level models.
